title: 2nd Stopping Place 5th Truth Universal And Particular Order And Wisdom Indicating An All Powerful All Wise One

questions.question: What main quality of the universe is described in the first paragraph of the passage?
questions.answer: A careful and wise order is described in everything, from the largest parts of the universe to the smallest parts of human life.

questions.question: What examples are given to show that this order appears in both large and small things?
questions.answer: The passage mentions the overall plan of the universe, the earth’s daily and yearly movement, a human face, the senses in the head, and blood cells.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of being can truly act on things in a deliberate and creative way?
questions.answer: Only One who has complete power and complete wisdom can do that.

questions.question: How are created things described compared with the One who orders them?
questions.answer: They are described as receivers of what is done to them, places where power appears, and not active controllers on their own.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect order with knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice?
questions.answer: Because arranging things for clear purposes and benefits requires understanding and intentional decision-making.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how things come into existence, take a state, and receive a form?
questions.answer: They are brought into being by divine power, given their condition by divine will, and shaped by divine choice.

questions.question: In the section about the world as a hospice, what idea is repeated many times with the word “one”?
questions.answer: The passage keeps showing that major parts of the world’s system are single, which points to oneness in its Maker.

questions.question: What does the repeated oneness of the world’s provisions and systems prove about its Maker?
questions.answer: It shows that the Maker is one and that He is very generous and welcoming to living beings.

questions.question: What is meant by saying great officials are employed to serve the guests of this hospice?
questions.answer: It means powerful created means are used to provide for living creatures in the world.

questions.question: Which divine Names or attributes are mentioned as being seen everywhere?
questions.answer: The passage mentions Names such as All-Wise, Compassionate, Giver of Forms, Disposer, Quickener, and Nurturer, along with qualities like wisdom, mercy, and grace.

questions.question: What does it mean that these Names and acts “embrace every place”?
questions.answer: It means their effects can be seen throughout the world and are not limited to only one area.

questions.question: How do the divine Names and acts relate to one another in the passage?
questions.answer: They work together so closely that their effects appear united and harmonious.

questions.question: What example is given to show that many divine Names appear together in one thing?
questions.answer: When life is given to something, other actions like creating, shaping, and providing also appear at the same time.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from the same Names and acts appearing everywhere in the same system?
questions.answer: The One described by those Names and the Doer of those acts must be one, single, and unique.

questions.question: What response does the passage give at the end to this truth?
questions.answer: It declares belief in this truth and full acceptance of it.

questions.question: What central claim does this passage make about the order found in the world?
questions.answer: It says that the order of the world shows there is one Creator who acts with wisdom, will, and power.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observing nature to speaking about the Creator?
questions.answer: It points to the pattern, purpose, and balance in creation and then says such order must come from a knowing and choosing Maker.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both the movement of the earth and the cells in human blood?
questions.answer: To show that the same careful order exists at every level, from huge systems to tiny details.

questions.question: What idea is taught by saying no other being can intentionally and creatively interfere with things?
questions.answer: It teaches that real control belongs only to Allah, while created things do not have independent creative power.

questions.question: What is the meaning of calling other things passive?
questions.answer: It means they do not create by themselves but are acted upon.

questions.question: Why would regularity aimed at benefits require will and choice?
questions.answer: Because useful and purposeful arrangement does not happen blindly; it must be intended.

questions.question: According to the passage, what three divine qualities are especially tied to creation here?
questions.answer: Power, will, and choice.

questions.question: In the world-as-hospice example, what does the image of hospitality help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see the world as a place where living beings are cared for and provided for by a generous Lord.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the lamp, time-marker, drink, and field of the world are each one?
questions.answer: It suggests that many basic parts of the world operate in unified ways, pointing back to one Master.

questions.question: How does generosity connect with oneness in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: The same one Maker who runs the world also provides many blessings for its living guests.

questions.question: What is the role of the divine Names listed in the fourth paragraph?
questions.answer: They describe different ways Allah’s actions and qualities appear throughout creation.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says those Names and deeds are present everywhere?
questions.answer: Their signs and effects are found across the whole world.

questions.question: How do the Names support each other according to the passage?
questions.answer: Their effects match and complete one another so perfectly that they seem woven together.

questions.question: What example shows that giving life is not an isolated action?
questions.answer: When something receives life, it is also created, formed, and provided for at the same time.

questions.question: What final belief is supported by all these examples?
questions.answer: That the One acting throughout creation is one, unique, and without partner.

questions.question: In simple terms, what does the first paragraph say about the universe?
questions.answer: It says the universe is arranged with amazing care and purpose.

questions.question: What human examples are used to make this idea easier to understand?
questions.answer: The passage points to a person’s face, senses, and blood circulation.

questions.question: What can students infer from the passage’s use of both cosmic and human examples?
questions.answer: They can infer that the same wisdom governs everything, no matter the size.

questions.question: What kind of action is denied to anything other than the One described in the passage?
questions.answer: Deliberate and creative control over things is denied to anything else.

questions.question: If created things are only receivers and places where action appears, what does that tell us about their limits?
questions.answer: It tells us they do not independently produce the order we see.

questions.question: Why is knowledge necessary for setting things in order for useful results?
questions.answer: Because useful planning depends on knowing what each thing needs and what result is intended.

questions.question: Why is choice necessary, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because giving each thing a special condition and form requires selecting one possibility over another.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the source of every created thing’s specific form?
questions.answer: Its specific form comes through divine choice.

questions.question: What picture of the world is created by calling it a hospice?
questions.answer: It presents the world as a place of care, provision, and hosting.

questions.question: How does the long list of single things in the world support the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: It builds the idea that a unified world points to a single Lord behind it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the character of the Maker besides His oneness?
questions.answer: It says He is very generous and caring toward living creatures.

questions.question: Why are several divine Names listed instead of only one?
questions.answer: To show that many different kinds of mercy, wisdom, life-giving, and arranging are all active in the world.

questions.question: What does it mean that each Name and act is found in every place “in the utmost degree”?
questions.answer: It means their signs appear broadly and powerfully throughout creation.

questions.question: How does the example of giving life strengthen the idea of divine unity?
questions.answer: It shows that many coordinated actions happen together under one system, so they come from one Doer.

questions.question: What attitude should a believer have at the end of this passage?
questions.answer: A believer should accept this truth with faith and agreement.

questions.question: What is one major sign in creation that the passage uses as evidence for divine unity?
questions.answer: The passage uses the precise order found everywhere in creation as a major sign.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this order is not random?
questions.answer: It says the order serves purposes and brings benefits, which shows intention.

questions.question: What kinds of things are included in this order?
questions.answer: Both the whole universe and small details in human beings are included.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only an absolutely powerful and wise One can reach every thing in this way?
questions.answer: Because controlling all levels of existence with purpose and precision requires unlimited power and wisdom.

questions.question: What opposite picture is given about created things?
questions.answer: They are shown as dependent and acted upon rather than as independent makers.

questions.question: What does the passage say is required for true ordering?
questions.answer: It requires knowledge, wisdom, will, and choice.

questions.question: How does this requirement help prove the Creator is not without will?
questions.answer: Since the world shows purposeful arrangement, its Creator must choose intentionally rather than act blindly.

questions.question: What are the three stages described for created things: existence, state, and form?
questions.answer: They come into existence by power, receive their condition by will, and take shape by choice.

questions.question: In the hospitality example, what does the passage imply about the world’s resources?
questions.answer: It implies they are arranged like provisions prepared for guests.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase about things being “one” mainly point to?
questions.answer: It mainly points to the oneness of the world’s Lord.

questions.question: Besides oneness, what other quality of the Maker is stressed in that paragraph?
questions.answer: His generosity and hospitality are stressed.

questions.question: What do the divine Names in the next paragraph help us notice?
questions.answer: They help us notice the many ways Allah’s care and action appear throughout the world.

questions.question: How are the divine attributes and acts related in the passage?
questions.answer: They are unified and work in harmony everywhere.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example where life appears along with shaping and providing?
questions.answer: The lesson is that different acts in creation are linked under one command and one Actor.

questions.question: What final conclusion is stated openly in the last sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that the One shown by these Names and acts is one, single, and unique, and this is believed and affirmed.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be seen from the largest system down to the smallest detail?
questions.answer: A precise and meaningful order can be seen everywhere.

questions.question: Name two large-scale examples and two small-scale examples from the passage.
questions.answer: Large examples include the universe’s overall system and the earth’s movements; small examples include the human face and blood cells.

questions.question: What claim does the passage make about who can truly direct and create?
questions.answer: It says only one absolutely powerful and wise being can truly do that.

questions.question: How does the passage describe everything else besides that One?
questions.answer: It describes everything else as receiving action rather than originating it.

questions.question: Why is benefit important in the passage’s argument about order?
questions.answer: Because beneficial order shows that things are arranged purposefully, not meaninglessly.

questions.question: What mental qualities must exist for purposeful order to happen?
questions.answer: Knowledge and wisdom must exist.

questions.question: What personal qualities must exist for choosing one form and state over another?
questions.answer: Will and choice must exist.

questions.question: How does the passage connect these qualities to the Creator of all beings?
questions.answer: It says the Creator has power, will, and choice, and these are seen in how things are made.

questions.question: What is the effect of repeating the word “one” for many parts of the world’s system?
questions.answer: It makes the reader notice unity in the world and points to one Maker behind it.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the Maker’s treatment of living creatures?
questions.answer: It teaches that He cares for them generously like honored guests.

questions.question: Why might the passage mention many officials serving the guests?
questions.answer: To show that many created means are used in an organized way under one Lord’s command.

questions.question: What are some of the Names that show up across the whole world?
questions.answer: Among them are All-Wise, Compassionate, Giver of Forms, Quickener, Disposer, and Nurturer.

questions.question: What does it mean that these Names and deeds are seen in every corner of the world?
questions.answer: It means their effects are widespread and universal.

questions.question: According to the example in the last paragraph, what appears together when life is given?
questions.answer: Creating, shaping, and providing appear together with giving life.

questions.question: What does the passage want the reader to affirm after thinking about all this?
questions.answer: That the Doer behind all these acts is one unique Lord.

questions.question: What truth about creation is emphasized first in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage first emphasizes that all creation shows exact and wise order.

questions.question: How does the passage use the human body to support this truth?
questions.answer: It points to the face, senses, and blood circulation as examples of detailed order.

questions.question: How does it use the wider universe to support the same truth?
questions.answer: It refers to the whole plan of the cosmos and the regular movement of the earth.

questions.question: What reason is given for saying that no one except the One described can truly act creatively on things?
questions.answer: Because such action requires absolute power and wisdom.

questions.question: What three words describe the role of created things in relation to divine action?
questions.answer: They are described as receivers, places where action is shown, and passive.

questions.question: Why can’t regularity aimed at benefits come from blind accident, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because aiming at benefits requires understanding and intention.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the difference between power, will, and choice?
questions.answer: Power brings things into existence, will gives them a certain condition, and choice gives them a specific form.

questions.question: What is the main lesson from the examples of the world’s lamp, time-marker, drink, and field?
questions.answer: These examples teach that the world works as a unified place under one Master.

questions.question: What does the passage say this unity tells us about the Maker’s character?
questions.answer: It tells us He is one and very generous in caring for living beings.

questions.question: What is the purpose of listing divine Names like Quickener and Nurturer?
questions.answer: The purpose is to show different divine actions appearing throughout creation.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying these Names, attributes, and acts are all one?
questions.answer: It means they belong to one divine source and work together in complete harmony.

questions.question: How do the Names support one another instead of conflicting?
questions.answer: Their effects fit together so perfectly that each one strengthens the others.

questions.question: Why is the example of giving life especially strong evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: Because life appears together with many other coordinated acts at the same moment and in the same system.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the same pattern appearing everywhere?
questions.answer: It can be inferred that one single Doer is behind all of it.

questions.question: How does the passage end in terms of faith and response?
questions.answer: It ends by saying this truth is believed and accepted wholeheartedly.
